{{short description|Chinese molecular biologist (born 1938)}}
{{family name hatnote|[[Hong (Chinese surname)|Hong]]|lang=Chinese}}

'''Hong Guofan''' ({{lang-zh|s=洪国藩}}; born December 1938), or '''Guo-Fan Hong''', is a Chinese molecular biologist and professor of the [[Shanghai Institute of Biochemistry and Cell Biology]]. He served as Director of the National Center for Gene Research of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS). He is an academician of the CAS and of [[The World Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.hlhl.org.cn/english/showsub.asp?id=272|title=Hong Guofan|date=|publisher=HLHL Foundation|access-date=2018-06-18}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Hong was born in December 1938 in [[Ningbo]], [[Zhejiang]] Province. He graduated from [[Fudan University]] in [[Shanghai]] in 1964 and worked at the Shanghai Institute of Biochemistry afterwards.<ref name=":0" /> On the recommendations of professors [[Wang Yinglai]] and [[Wang Debao]], Hong became a research fellow under Nobel laureate [[Frederick Sanger]] at [[Cambridge University]]'s [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] in 1979.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://news.sciencenet.cn/htmlnews/2013/12/286524.shtm|title=洪国藩院士撰文：纪念恩师桑格|last=Hong|first=Guofan|date=2013-12-20|website=Sciencenet.cn|access-date=2018-06-18}}</ref> He returned to China after Sanger's retirement in 1983.<ref name=":1" /> In 1990, Hong requested Sanger's assistance in creating a Chinese Sequencing Unit to contribute to [[Human Genome Project]]. Sanger contacted [[James Watson]] endorsing Hong's expertise. However, Watson rebuffed the offer due to the treatment of Chinese students in the [[1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre|1989 Tiananmen Square Massacre]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sanger, Fred |url=https://wellcomecollection.org/works/mg57j542/items |access-date=2025-10-09 |website=Wellcome Collection |language=en}}</ref> Hong was elected as an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1997.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.casad.cas.cn/aca/374/smkxhyxxb-200906-t20090624_1803295.html|title=洪国藩 |publisher=Chinese Academy of Sciences |access-date=2018-06-18}}</ref>

Hong's research is focused on DNA and [[genome]] science. He designed the "rapid and accurate [[Bacterial artificial chromosome|BAC]]-fingerprinting-anchoring strategy", which facilitated the BAC-config mapping of the rice genome.<ref name=":0" /> For his contributions he was awarded the [[Ho Leung Ho Lee Prize]] in life sciences.<ref name=":0" />
